test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 14 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In a circle, chords AB and CD are produced to meet at E. outside the circle. If AB = 9 cm and AE = 12 cm and ED = 4 cm, then what is the length of the chord CD?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the **External Secant Segment Theorem**, when two secants are drawn from an external point to a circle, the product of the length of one secant and its external part equals the product of the length of the other secant and its external part.

Logic: EA × EB = EC × ED

Given: EA = 12 cm, AB = 9 cm ⇒ EB = AE − AB = 12 − 9 = 3 cm

Also: ED = 4 cm, EC = ED + CD = 4 + CD

⇒ 12 × 3 = 4 × (4 + CD)

⇒ 36 = 16 + 4 × CD ⇒ 4 × CD = 20 ⇒ CD = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of secant segment **AE** = 12 cm

Length of chord **AB** = 9 cm

Length of external part **ED** = 4 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Intersecting Secants Theorem:** EA × EB = EC × ED

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/835c0f8a776f28edc0a546eab12a30bdc084b4afc1f3f3af724c00d0f3235fe7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ EB = AE − AB

⇒ EB = 12 − 9 = 3 cm

⇒ According to the theorem: EA × EB = EC × ED

⇒ 12 × 3 = EC × 4

⇒ 36 = EC × 4

⇒ EC = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm

⇒ We know that EC = ED + CD

⇒ 9 = 4 + CD

⇒ CD = 9 − 4 = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Internal Chord Theorem

If two chords AB and CD intersect inside a circle at point P, then PA × PB = PC × PD.

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent segment ET and a secant segment EAB are drawn from an external point E, then ET² = EA × EB.

Power of a Point

For a point E at distance d from the center of a circle with radius r, the value d² − r² is constant for any line through E and is equal to the product of the segments of any secant.</p
